One-time opt-in to private skill indexing for a skill inventory. Guarded by the inventory's SCM connection readiness check. Returns 422 when the connection is not ready — the error message is the machine-readable, provider-namespaced reason (e.g. github_app_not_installed, github_app_account_mismatch, github_app_unhealthy for GitHub; bitbucket_not_connected, bitbucket_reconnect_required, bitbucket_workspace_mismatch for Bitbucket; gitlab_not_connected, gitlab_scope_mismatch for GitLab) — and 409 (already_opted_in) when the inventory has already opted in. On success it asynchronously starts the private skill indexing workflow for the latest scan (if any).

Re-triggers private skill indexing for the latest scan of a workspace-scoped skill inventory. Only valid once the inventory has opted in to private indexing (409 not_opted_in otherwise) and when a scan exists to index (409 no_scan_to_reindex otherwise). The trigger is idempotent per scan: if a run for the latest scan is already in flight it returns status 'already_running' rather than starting a second one.

get.description: Paginated list of the inventory's pending first-party logical skills still awaiting an approval decision, scoped to the latest scan. Each row carries the skill's name, description and footprint (repo/instance counts). Sortable by canonical name or repo.

post.description: Approves a selection of the inventory's pending first-party logical skills, assigning each to a target workspace, and triggers private indexing of the latest scan so the newly approved skills are indexed. Each item's target workspace must be one the actor may assign skills to (edit permission) and must belong to the same org as the inventory owner; a 404 is returned for one that is not editable and a 400 (workspace_cross_org) for one in another org. Duplicate logicalSkillId entries are rejected (400 duplicate_skills). Indexing is only triggered once the inventory has opted into private indexing — approvals are still recorded otherwise (attributes.indexing = "skipped"). Approvals are durable once committed: if starting the indexing workflow fails the request still succeeds and attributes.indexing reports "unavailable" or "failed" so the client can retry indexing without re-approving.

put.description: Updates the inventory's indexing preferences. Only the supplied fields are written, so `autoApproveNewSkills` and `defaultTargetWorkspaceId` can be changed independently. The route only starts the workflow; the scan, persist, and follow-up indexing run inside it.

Returns 400 when the workspace has no connected integration for the provider, 409 when a scan or analysis is already in flight, 503 when the workflow engine could not accept the scan, and 404 when the onboarding feature flag is off. Returns the inventory id and the dispatched scan index so the UI can navigate to the progress screen. The route only starts the workflow; the scan, persist, and analysis run inside it.

skill.description: The plugin to install and the skill to run. A value without a `file:` prefix means a registry ref (either a full `workspace/plugin[@version]` or a bare `plugin[@version]` name resolved across the workspaces the caller can see); a value with a `file:` prefix means a local plugin path inside the cloned repo (e.g. file:apps/cli/plugins/agent-enablement). Either form may carry a trailing `#skill` selector (e.g. `workspace/plugin@1.0.0#implement-ticket` or `file:apps/cli/plugins/agent-enablement#implement-ticket`) that installs the whole plugin and launches the one named skill; it is required when the plugin exposes more than one skill. This is a wire convention: the value is stored verbatim and interpreted downstream by the launch recipe.

snapshot.description: Commit SHA or tag pinning the repo snapshot for this run. Pins the checked-out repository, not the sandbox runtime image — use `sandboxSnapshot` for the latter.

sandboxSnapshot.description: Operational override selecting the sandbox runtime image the launch run is created from. Distinct from `snapshot`, which pins the checked-out repository. When omitted the run falls back to the configured default.

encryptedEnvUpload.description: Reference to an encrypted-input upload (e.g. an env-file) delivered to the launch sandbox. Must be an existing, viewable, encrypted upload. Mutually exclusive with `environmentId`.

environmentId.description: Id of a workspace environment whose sealed `.env` payload is opened server-side at launch and delivered to the sandbox. Must belong to the launch workspace. A live reference resolved when each run starts, so environment edits affect subsequently started and resumed runs and a deleted environment fails the launch. Mutually exclusive with `encryptedEnvUpload`.

uploads.description: Additional upload keys (context archives, config tarballs) keyed by a caller-defined logical name. Each must be an existing, viewable upload.

inputs.description: Skill-specific inputs forwarded to the launched skill, keyed by the skill's own placeholder names (e.g. ISSUE_IDENTIFIER, ISSUE_TITLE, ISSUE_DESCRIPTION).

instructions.description: Free-text instructions appended to the skill prompt the launch agent runs, mirroring the local `--instructions` flag. Distinct from the structured `inputs` channel.

get.description: Lists launch runs in the workspaces the caller can view, newest-first.

post.description: Resumes a completed launch run: creates a new child run that reruns the CloudLaunch recipe with the parent run’s workspace restored, so the launch agent continues its prior session.

instructions.description: Free-text instructions for the resumed run. Overrides the parent run’s instructions when supplied; omitted keeps the parent’s.

get.description: Gets a launch run by ID, including progress while pending and a failure reason when failed.

Returns the raw provider JSONL transcript for a launch run's agent logs. Serves the most recently captured session as a single transcript; `204 No Content` means no session has been uploaded (or its upload has not completed) yet.

post.description: Creates a named, workspace-scoped environment. The supplied `.env` payload is validated, sealed under the workspace key, and never returned by any read path.

envFile.description: Raw `.env` file contents (`KEY=VALUE` per line). Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored. Mutually exclusive with `entries`.

entries.description: Environment variables as a `KEY=VALUE` map. Mutually exclusive with `envFile`.

get.description: Lists environments in the workspaces the caller can view, newest-first. Never returns the sealed values — only names, metadata, and declared key names.
Gets a single environment by ID (metadata only — the sealed value is never returned).

put.description: Replaces an environment's sealed value in place. The new `.env` payload is validated, sealed under the workspace key, and never returned.

envFile.description: Raw `.env` file contents (`KEY=VALUE` per line). Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored. Mutually exclusive with `entries`.

entries.description: Environment variables as a `KEY=VALUE` map. Mutually exclusive with `envFile`.

delete.description: Deletes an environment by ID.

get.description: Gets the reviewer plugin configuration for a workspace.

put.description: Sets the reviewer plugin configuration for a workspace.

delete.description: Deletes the reviewer plugin configuration for a workspace.

get.description: Lists tile-skills (skills shipped inside a tile version) sourced from a given repository URL.

post.description: Create-or-get a task by `idempotencyKey`. Emits `task.created`; when `startImmediately` (default true) and inputs are supplied, kicks off the first run.

get.description: List tasks in a workspace, optionally filtered by status.
Find a task by its (workspace, link type, link value) triple. 404 when no match exists.
Get a task by id, including its current run, pending-input count, links, and the latest event tail.
List events for a task, ordered ascending by id. Filterable by event type(s) and/or runId.

post.description: Write a client-emitted task event (`user_input.received`, `input.requested`, `run.progress`). Backend-owned lifecycle events (`task.created`, `run.*`, `task.cancelled`) MUST be rejected with 400.
Thin sugar over POST /tasks/{id}/events that fires exactly one `user_input.received`.

get.description: List a task's `launch_run`s newest-first, each with status, failureReason, extracted links, the `run.created`/`run.completed` event ids, and its `resumeOfLaunchRunId` lineage.

post.description: Cancel a task: terminates the current run's Temporal workflow (if any), emits `task.cancelled`, and sets status to `cancelled`.

get.description: Workspace-wide task-event feed. Same item shape as `GET /tasks/{id}/events`. Filterable by event type(s), taskId, or a `since` timestamp.
Deprecated — replaced by GET /capacity-lease. Lists active sandbox leases for safe rollback.

delete.description: Deprecated — replaced by DELETE /capacity-lease. Truncates all active sandbox leases.

post.description: Deprecated — replaced by POST /capacity-lease/:leaseId/stop. Stops the sandbox attached to a running lease.

get.description: Lists commits on a repository's default branch via the workspace's SCM integration. Supports keyword/author/date filtering.
